# InjectKit

> Lightweight, type-safe dependency injection container for TypeScript. ESM-only.
> Build a registry, register services with a fluent API, call `build()` to validate
> the graph, then resolve from the returned container.

This file is a complete, self-contained reference written for LLMs and coding agents.
Everything below is accurate for the installed version; prefer it over guessing from
general DI knowledge, because several of InjectKit's rules differ from other containers.

## Install

```bash
npm install injectkit
```

ESM-only. No CommonJS or UMD build. Requires Node >= 22.

## Required setup (read this first)

Constructor injection will not work without the right toolchain config. This is the most
common failure and it fails **silently** (resolution produces `undefined` dependencies)
rather than raising a clear error.

Two options:

**Option A (portable): declare deps explicitly.** Works with any toolchain, no reflection
metadata needed. Use this when you cannot rely on emitted metadata, such as browser
builds and bundlers that strip it.

```typescript
@Injectable({ deps: [Logger, Database] })
class UserService {
  constructor(
    private logger: Logger,
    private db: Database,
  ) {}
}
```

**Option B (recommended): rely on emitted metadata.** Keeps the decorator free of a
dependency list that has to stay in sync with the constructor signature.

```typescript
@Injectable()
class UserService {
  constructor(private logger: Logger) {}
}
```

This requires `tsconfig.json` with both `"experimentalDecorators": true` and
`"emitDecoratorMetadata": true`, plus `import 'reflect-metadata'` once at your entry
point. Bundlers and test runners need a transform that preserves decorator metadata (e.g.
`unplugin-swc` for Vite/Vitest). If any of that is missing, resolution silently produces
`undefined` dependencies, so verify the setup before assuming a wiring bug. Explicit
`deps` always take priority when both are present, so you can mix the two and migrate
gradually.

**`@Injectable()` does nothing at runtime.** It is an identity decorator whose only job
is to record metadata. Omitting it on a class that uses constructor injection breaks
resolution silently. Every class with constructor dependencies needs it (or one of the
lifetime decorators below, which imply it).

## Minimal complete example

```typescript
import 'reflect-metadata'; // once, at your entry point
import { createRegistry, Injectable } from 'injectkit';

@Injectable()
class Logger {
  log(message: string) {
    console.log(message);
  }
}

@Injectable()
class UserService {
  constructor(private logger: Logger) {}

  createUser(name: string) {
    this.logger.log(`creating ${name}`);
  }
}

const registry = createRegistry();
registry.register(Logger).useClass(Logger).asSingleton();
registry.register(UserService).useClass(UserService).asSingleton();

const container = registry.build(); // validates the graph, throws on problems
container.get(UserService).createUser('ada');
```

## API

### Entry points

| Export                 | Signature                                            | Notes                            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `createRegistry`       | `(metadataRegistry?: MetadataRegistry) => InjectKitRegistry` | Preferred way to make a registry |
| `InjectKitRegistry`    | `new (metadataRegistry?: MetadataRegistry)`          | Same thing as a class            |
| `InjectKitContainerNoop` | `new ()`                                           | Null-object container; every `get()` throws, `override()` is a no-op, `hasRegistration()` is always `false` |

### Registry

| Method                        | Returns              | Notes                                          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `register<T>(id)`             | `RegistrationType<T>` | `id` is a class, abstract class, string, or symbol. Throws if already registered. |
| `registerValue<T>(token, v)`  | `this`               | `token` must be a string or symbol. Always a singleton. |
| `remove<T>(id)`               | `void`               | Throws if not registered.                      |
| `isRegistered<T>(id)`         | `boolean`            |                                                |
| `build(options?)`             | `Container`          | Validates, then returns the container.         |

### Creation strategies (pick exactly one per registration)

| Method                  | Then                    | Notes                                        |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `.useClass(Ctor)`       | `.asSingleton()` etc.   | Constructor injection.                       |
| `.useFactory(fn)`       | `.asSingleton()` etc.   | `fn: (container: Container) => T`.           |
| `.useInstance(obj)`     | terminal                | **Always singleton**, lifetime calls ignored. |
| `.useValue(v)`          | terminal                | **Always singleton**. Use for primitives, `undefined`, falsy values. |
| `.useArray(Ctor)`       | `.push(id)`             | Collects several tokens into an array. `Ctor` must `extends Array<V>`. |
| `.useMap(Ctor)`         | `.set(key, id)`         | Collects several tokens into a map. `Ctor` must `extends Map<K, V>`. |

### Lifetimes

| Method           | Behavior                                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.asSingleton()` | One instance for the whole container tree, cached at the root. |
| `.asScoped()`    | One instance per scope, shared down the scope's children. |
| `.asTransient()` | New instance on every `get()`. **This is the default.**  |

### Container

| Method                    | Notes                                                     |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get<T>(id): T`           | Throws if the id is not registered or the container is disposed. |
| `hasRegistration<T>(id)`  | `boolean`.                                                |
| `createScopedContainer()` | Returns a `ScopedContainer` (a `Container` plus `override`). Throws if the container is disposed. |
| `override<T>(id, inst)`   | Substitutes an instance. Available on scopes and on the container `build()` returns, not on a `Container` injected into a service. |
| `disposeAsync()`          | Idempotent. Also available via `await using`.             |

### Decorators

| Decorator                  | Effect                                                    |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@Injectable(options?)`    | Marks the class injectable. No default lifetime.           |
| `@Singleton(options?)`     | Injectable, defaults to singleton.                         |
| `@Scoped(options?)`        | Injectable, defaults to scoped.                            |
| `@Transient(options?)`     | Injectable, defaults to transient.                         |
| `@Provider(id, options?)`  | Declares the token this class satisfies during auto-registration. |

`options` is `{ deps?: readonly Identifier<unknown>[] }`, in constructor parameter order.
A lifetime set by decorator is a default; the fluent API overrides it.

### build(options)

```typescript
container = registry.build({
  // false (default) | true | Class[]
  autoRegisterDecorated: [Logger, UserService],
  overrides: [
    { token: Logger, useClass: TestLogger, lifetime: 'singleton' },
    { token: Clock, useFactory: () => fixedClock },
    { token: CONFIG, useValue: { debug: true } },
  ],
});
```

Composition order: explicit registrations win over decorated ones, the automatic
`Container` registration only fills a gap, and `overrides` are applied last so they can
replace anything.

Prefer the array form of `autoRegisterDecorated`. The default metadata registry is
process-global, so `true` can pull in decorated classes from unrelated modules. For hard
isolation, pass a fresh `new DefaultMetadataRegistry()` to `createRegistry()`.

## Collections

Register several implementations behind one token. The token class must extend the
built-in it collects, or the return type resolves to `never` and the chain will not
compile.

```typescript
@Injectable()
class Handlers extends Array<Handler> {}

registry.register(JsonHandler).useClass(JsonHandler).asSingleton();
registry.register(XmlHandler).useClass(XmlHandler).asSingleton();
registry.register(Handlers).useArray(Handlers).push(JsonHandler).push(XmlHandler);

container.get(Handlers); // [JsonHandler, XmlHandler], in push order
```

```typescript
@Injectable()
class Processors extends Map<string, Processor> {}

registry.register(Processors).useMap(Processors).set('fast', FastProcessor).set('accurate', AccurateProcessor);

container.get(Processors).get('fast'); // FastProcessor instance
```

Each pushed or set token must itself be registered; the collection resolves them through
the container like any other dependency, so missing ones are reported by `build()`.

## Rules that differ from other DI containers

These are the ones to get right; they are where incorrect code usually comes from.

1. **The default lifetime is transient**, not singleton. Always state the lifetime you
   want.
2. **`useInstance` and `useValue` are always singletons**, regardless of any lifetime
   call on the same registration.
3. **Validation happens at `build()`, not at `get()`.** Missing dependencies, circular
   dependencies, and captive dependencies all throw from `build()`.
4. **A singleton may not depend on a scoped registration.** `build()` rejects it. See
   "Captive dependencies" below.
5. **Singletons resolve their dependencies from the root container**, even when the
   `get()` that constructs one comes from a scope. A singleton therefore never sees a
   scope's `override()` values. To stub a singleton's dependency, override on the root
   container.
6. **`Container` is auto-registered**, so any service can inject `Container` to resolve
   lazily. It is transient, so each service receives the container that resolved it. It
   is not an unregistered identifier; do not register it yourself unless you mean to
   replace it.
7. **Scoped instances cache on the scope that resolves them**; singletons bubble to the
   root. A child scope inherits a scoped instance an ancestor has *already created*, but
   a child that resolves first caches its own, and the parent then creates a separate
   one. Resolve at the level that owns the unit of work, not in a nested scope.
8. **Disposal is per-owner.** Disposing a scope releases only that scope's instances and
   never bubbles to the root; disposing the root releases singletons but does not reach
   into child scopes. Dispose each scope at the end of its unit of work. Only instances
   the container constructed are disposed, so `useInstance` and `useValue` values are
   left alone.

## Captive dependencies

A singleton is created once and cached at the root, so anything it holds lives just as
long. If that dependency is scoped, the singleton would freeze one scope's instance and
keep using it after that scope is disposed. `build()` rejects this:

```typescript
registry.register(RequestContext).useClass(RequestContext).asScoped();
registry.register(CacheService).useClass(CacheService).asSingleton(); // depends on RequestContext
registry.build();
// Error: Captive dependency: singleton CacheService depends on scoped RequestContext:
// CacheService -> RequestContext. ...
```

Fix it by making the dependency a singleton, or the dependent scoped. The check follows
transient links, so indirect captures are reported with the full path. Depending on a
transient is allowed: the transient is created once from the root and shared for the
singleton's lifetime.

The check cannot see through `useFactory`, since factories resolve by hand and declare no
dependencies. A singleton factory is handed the root container, which prevents the
accidental capture, but a factory that deliberately resolves a scoped token is on you.

## Scopes

```typescript
const scope = container.createScopedContainer();
try {
  const service = scope.get(RequestHandler);
  await service.handle();
} finally {
  await scope.disposeAsync();
}
```

Or with explicit resource management:

```typescript
await using scope = container.createScopedContainer();
```

## Disposal

Containers and scopes implement `AsyncDisposable`. A container disposes the instances it
constructed, in **reverse creation order**, so a service is torn down before the
dependencies it was built from.

```typescript
@Injectable()
class DbConnection {
  async [Symbol.asyncDispose]() {
    await this.pool.end();
  }
}

await using container = registry.build(); // or: await container.disposeAsync()
```

| Registration                                | Disposed?                                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `useClass` / `useFactory` (container-built) | Yes, if it implements a dispose protocol         |
| `useInstance` / `useValue` / overrides      | No, the caller owns the instance                 |
| Transient                                   | No, never tracked; the caller owns each instance |

Opting in is protocol-based: implement `[Symbol.asyncDispose]` (async) or
`[Symbol.dispose]` (sync). A plain `dispose()` method is **not** detected.

Disposal is idempotent. After a container is disposed, `get()` and
`createScopedContainer()` on it throw. See rule 8 for which container owns what.

## Browser usage

The package ships a browser ESM bundle at the `injectkit/browser` subpath export, usable
directly from `<script type="module">`.

Bundlers strip `emitDecoratorMetadata`, so browser code must use Option A from "Required
setup": declare dependencies explicitly with `@Injectable({ deps: [...] })`. Without a
decorator transform, apply the decorator as a plain call:

```javascript
import { Injectable, createRegistry } from 'injectkit/browser';

class UserService {
  constructor(logger) {
    this.logger = logger;
  }
}
Injectable({ deps: [Logger] })(UserService);
```

## Metadata registry

Decorators record metadata in a `MetadataRegistry`. `createRegistry()` uses the
process-global default, reachable via `getDefaultMetadataRegistry()`.

That default is shared across every module in the process, which is why
`autoRegisterDecorated: true` can pull in decorated classes you did not intend. For hard
isolation, most often in tests, hand a fresh registry to `createRegistry`:

```typescript
import { createRegistry, DefaultMetadataRegistry } from 'injectkit';

const registry = createRegistry(new DefaultMetadataRegistry());
// sees only classes decorated after this point through this registry
```

`MetadataRegistry` is an interface (`defineServiceMetadata`, `getServiceMetadata`,
`getDecoratedClasses`, `getConstructorDependencies`), so a custom implementation can
replace the reflection strategy entirely. `ServiceMetadata` is the stored shape:
`{ injectable, lifetime?, provide?, deps? }`.

## Testing

Two approaches, both first-class:

```typescript
// 1. Build-time overrides: swap an implementation for the whole container.
const container = registry.build({
  overrides: [{ token: EmailService, useValue: mockEmail }],
});

// 2. Scope overrides: swap per test, leaving the root untouched.
const scope = container.createScopedContainer();
scope.override(EmailService, mockEmail);
```

Remember rule 5: a scope override is invisible to singletons. If the service under test
is a singleton, use a build-time override, or call `override` on the container `build()`
returned (it is a `ScopedContainer`, so this type-checks).

## Error messages and what they mean

| Message                                            | Cause                                               | Fix                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `Missing dependencies for X: Y`                    | `Y` is injected but never registered.                | Register `Y`, or add it via `overrides`.         |
| `Circular dependency found: A -> B -> A`           | A dependency cycle.                                  | Break the cycle, or inject `Container` and resolve lazily. |
| `Captive dependency: singleton X depends on scoped Y` | A singleton would outlive a scoped instance.      | Change one of the two lifetimes.                 |
| `Service dependency metadata unavailable: X`       | `X` has constructor params but no metadata at all.   | Check `emitDecoratorMetadata` and the `reflect-metadata` import, or add explicit `deps`. |
| `Service dependencies incomplete: X`               | `deps` array is shorter than the constructor's parameter list. | List every constructor parameter in `deps`, in order. |
| `Service dependency metadata incomplete: X`        | Reflected metadata exists but doesn't cover every parameter. | Usually a missing transform. Switch to explicit `deps`. |
| `Registration for X already exists`                | `register()` called twice for one id.                | Use `remove()` first, or a build override.       |
| `Registration for X not found`                     | Resolving an unregistered id.                        | Register it, or check `hasRegistration()` first. |
| `Invalid registration for X`                       | A registration with no creation strategy.            | Call one of `useClass` / `useFactory` / `useInstance` / `useValue`. |
| `Cannot resolve from a disposed container`         | `get()` after `disposeAsync()`.                      | Do not reuse a disposed scope.                   |
| `Cannot override a registration in a disposed container` | `override()` after `disposeAsync()`.           | Do not reuse a disposed scope.                   |
| `Cannot create a scope from a disposed container`  | `createScopedContainer()` after `disposeAsync()`.    | Do not reuse a disposed scope.                   |

## Type reference

```typescript
type Token = string | symbol;
type Identifier<T> = Constructor<T> | Abstract<T> | Token;
type Lifetime = 'singleton' | 'transient' | 'scoped';
type Factory<T> = (container: Container) => T;
type ScopedContainer = Container & { override<T>(id: Identifier<T>, instance: Instance<T>): void };
type Override<T> =
  | { token: Identifier<T>; useClass: Constructor<T>; lifetime?: Lifetime }
  | { token: Identifier<T>; useFactory: Factory<T>; lifetime?: Lifetime }
  | { token: Identifier<T>; useValue: Instance<T> };
type ServiceMetadata = {
  injectable: boolean;
  lifetime?: Lifetime;
  provide?: Identifier<unknown>;
  deps?: readonly Identifier<unknown>[];
};
```

`formatIdentifier(id)` is exported too; it renders an identifier the way the error
messages above do, which is useful when writing your own diagnostics.

`registry.build()` returns a `ScopedContainer`, so `override` is available on the root
container as well as on scopes.

Using a string or symbol token means `get()` cannot infer the type, so pass it:

```typescript
const LOGGER = Symbol('Logger');
registry.register<Logger>(LOGGER).useClass(ConsoleLogger).asSingleton();
const logger = container.get<Logger>(LOGGER);
```
